summary: BGP routers report problems with a NOTIFICATION message, and one error category covers the finite state machine (FSM). This RFC defines subcodes for it so operators get more detail about what went wrong and can correlate network events. It updates RFC 4271.

eli5.summary: When a machine shows only error, you have to guess. These extra codes are like the machine adding a note about which step went wrong.

subtitle: Gives BGP Finite State Machine errors subcodes that say which state saw an unexpected message.

tldr.problem: The BGP Finite State Machine Error code gave operators little detail for diagnosing problems.
tldr.mechanism: Subcodes 0 to 3 are defined, and a speaker that gets an unexpected message in OpenSent, OpenConfirm or Established MUST send a NOTIFICATION with the matching subcode.
tldr.outcome: Operators get more information, though the RFC warns it could make BGP implementation fingerprinting easier. It updates RFC 4271.

today: RFC 6608 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4271. The metadata lists no later RFC replacing or updating it.

sections.title: Why FSM Subcodes
sections.content: The subcodes help network operators diagnose BGP finite state machine (FSM) problems and correlate network events, and help developers in lab situations. The RFC updates RFC 4271 by requiring BGP implementations to insert appropriate FSM Error subcodes in NOTIFICATION messages.
sections.eli5: Extra detail on the error message helps people find the cause faster.

sections.title: The Subcodes
sections.content:
Four subcodes are defined for the Finite State Machine Error:

  • 0: Unspecified Error
  • 1: Receive Unexpected Message in OpenSent State
  • 2: Receive Unexpected Message in OpenConfirm State
  • 3: Receive Unexpected Message in Established State
sections.eli5: Each number names a different step where the surprise happened.

sections.title: How Speakers Use Them
sections.content:
If a speaker receives an unexpected message in OpenSent (for example KEEPALIVE, UPDATE or ROUTE-REFRESH), OpenConfirm (OPEN, UPDATE or ROUTE-REFRESH) or Established (for example OPEN), it MUST send a NOTIFICATION with the Finite State Machine Error code and the matching subcode.

The Data field is a 1-octet, unsigned integer indicating the type of the unexpected message.
sections.eli5: When a router gets a message at the wrong time, it tells its neighbor which step it was in and what message surprised it.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The subcodes could make BGP implementation fingerprinting easier and probably more accurate, which operators should consider as an operational security matter. IANA created the registry "BGP Finite State Machine Error Subcodes" with a Registration Procedure of "Standards Action", populated with values 0 to 3.
sections.eli5: More detail helps repairs, but it could also help someone guess which brand of router you use.
